payload.blocks: Closing phase 8 and, through it, phases 9 and 10. The in-footprint slice of phase 8 (the driver.rs test kill and the git and node PATH lookups) runs now.
payload.headline: Phase 8: allow own-child liveness polls and keep three missing-survivor copies as named debt, or build the survivors?

parts.cause: The first phase 8 unit read every site (report unit-261123-2333-p8-result.md). The polls watch long-lived children the file started itself; the rows' own reasons say they are not bounded runs, and moving them onto spawn.rs run_bounded changes deadlines, output limits and Windows Job Object ends. fgos-process has no winpid reader and holder-lock has no single-instance lock usable at addon load. The V7n module moves only when p-irt4weqipe re-measures it.

options.cost: No product code beyond the running slice; phase 10 edits the row (about 30 lines of YAML).
options.does: Phase 10 lists the own-child try_wait polls as allowed with a reason and count on run-bounded-child, since they are not copies of a bounded run. The V7n module (retiredBy p-irt4weqipe), the winpid read and the single_load flock stay named debt, each with a backlog item the supervisor opens.
options.gain: Phase 8 closes today with no behaviour change; the guard still catches any new bounded-run copy, because each allowed file has a count.
options.harm: The try_wait pattern guards less inside the allowed files; the named-debt list grows by three entries.
options.label: A. Allow the polls, name three debts

options.does: All remaining debts, polls included, stay as named debt with retiredBy the row's existing rule (when the crate next changes how it spawns) or a backlog item.
options.harm: Twelve or more debt files stay listed with no real retirement date; this is far from acceptance criterion 4.
options.label: B. Everything left is named debt

options.cost: About 2 to 4 days and 600 or more lines of Rust and tests; phases 9 and 10 wait.
options.does: The planner adds a phase that gives fgos-process a winpid reader, gives holder-lock a single-instance lock, and moves every poll onto spawn.rs.
options.gain: Criterion 4 met as written, with no named debt from phase 8.
options.harm: A behaviour change across six crates (deadlines, Job Objects, cancellation), and a wider footprint into packages/process/rust/src/spawn.rs and holder-lock.
options.label: C. Build the survivors in a new phase

parts.recommendation: A: the polls are not copies of a bounded run, so allowing them with a count is the honest guard; the three real gaps get their own items instead of being forced into this plan.

scope.allows: The lead closes phase 8 after the running slice lands; phase 10 adds the allowed entries and the three named debts; the supervisor opens backlog items for the winpid reader and the single-instance lock.
scope.forbids: Any change to spawn.rs, holder-lock or the V7n module in this plan, and any widening of the footprint.

parts.what: Phase 8 must leave no debt on four door rows. Two moves fit and are running now. The rest cannot move inside the footprint: 12 own-child try_wait polls (gateway, launch, supervise, herdr, containment, steps and others), the frozen V7n Node module (two rows), the borrow_vectors winpid read, and the macOS flock in the git addon's single_load.
